Rudrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157716922/ 1 High Court Of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench. ...Respondent (By Sri.Praveen K Uppar, Hcgp.) 2 This Petition Is Filed Under Section 482 Of Cr.P.C., Seeking To Quash The Charge Sheet And Entire Proceedings Initiated In C.C.No.457 Of 2017 On The File Of Iv Jmfc Court Belagavi In Pursuance Of Apmc Police Station Crime No.13 Of 2017 Registered By The Apmc Police Station, Belagavi For The Offences Punishable Under Sections 403 And 420 Read With Section 34 Of Ipc, So Far As It Relates To The Petitioners Herein. This Petition Coming On For Admission This Day, The Court Made The Following: Order
texts.facts: Though the matter is listed for admission, with the consent from both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal. 2. This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking to quash the charge sheet and the entire proceedings initiated in C.C.No.457/2017 on the file of IV JMFC, Belagavi. 3. The respondent-police have filed a charge sheet against four accused persons alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 403, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC. The substance of the accusations made in the charge sheet is that, on 21.01.2017 on credible information the PSI of CCIB Unit, Belagavi kept a watch near the APMC Market Yard and found two persons standing suspiciously holding a plastic bag on their shoulders. When the raiding team surrounded them, one of them escaped from the spot, whereas, petitioner No.1-Ganghadar @ Sanju S/o Rudrappa Hadaginhal was caught and on search he was found in possession of seven packets of milk powder weighing 1 Kg each and twelve packets weighing Kg each. Those packets were seized under a mahazar. A FIR was registered and after investigation, the charge sheet was laid against four accused persons alleging that all the four accused persons were involved in the sale of milk powder which was supplied by the Government under Ksheera Bhagya Scheme.
texts.arguments: 4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the allegations made against the petitioners do not attract the offences under Sections 403 or 420 of IPC. The material produced by the prosecution indicate that petitioner No.1 was found in possession of the milk powder. The possession of the said milk powder is not an offence under any provisions of law much less under Sections 403 or 420 of IPC. There are no allegations whatsoever attracting the offence under Section 420 of IPC. Insofar as the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are concerned, there is absolutely no material to show their involvement in the alleged offences. Considering the very same material, this Court has Shri Ganghadar @ Sanju S/O. Rudrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157716922/ 2 already [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings in respect of accused No.4 in Criminal Petition No.101472/2017. The present petitioners also stand at par with accused No.4 against whom identical allegations are made. The prosecution of the petitioners therefore is wholly illegal and sheer abuse of the process of Court and hence, the learned counsel seeks for quashing the said proceedings. 5. Learned HCGP fairly concedes that the prosecution has not collected any material insofar as the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are concerned in order to support the accusations made against them for the alleged offences under Sections 403 and 420 of IPC. However, insofar as petitioner No.1 namely accused No.1 is concerned, he submits that the investigation conducted by the prosecution reveal that he was in possession of milk packets which were not meant for sale in the market. The sale of milk powder supplied under the schemes formulated by the Government is an offence and therefore, the prosecution of petitioner No.1 is in accordance with law and no illegallity or abuse of process of law is involved in the instant case sofar as accused No.1 is concerned and hence seeks for dismissal of the petition.
